source: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 16 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 16
knowledgePattern: Transform integral intervals before comparing exponential heights
solution:
Move each graph to the same unit interval, preserving its area. A horizontal translation gives X=∫012udu. For Y, double the widths to move the interval to 0 to 1, then halve the heights to keep the area unchanged. Halving the heights removes the outside factor 2, giving Y=∫012udu.

For Z, translate the interval one unit to the right, then halve the widths to fit 0 to 1. Double the heights to keep the area unchanged; this removes the outside factor one half, leaving Z=∫01(2)udu=∫012u/2du. Also W=∫0122udu.

For 0<u<1, u/2<u<u<2u. Exponentiation with base 2 preserves this order. The integrands are strictly ordered throughout the open unit interval, so their integrals satisfy Z<Y<X<W. Answer A.

hints.title: Give the areas the same interval
hints.body: Sketch the region for X. Move its graph one unit left so that its interval becomes 0 to 1.
hints.recap: A sideways translation keeps area unchanged.
hints.pitfall: Move the integration limits with the graph.
hints.pause: Write X as an integral from 0 to 1.

recall.reminder: Track how a translation changes a graph’s input and interval.

hints.title: Keep track of the change in width
hints.body: Move Z’s interval one unit right. Then stretch or shrink the intervals for Y and Z to width 1, adjusting the outside multiplier to preserve each area.
hints.recap: Multiplying every width by a factor multiplies area by that factor.
hints.pitfall: A horizontal stretch without an area adjustment changes the integral.
hints.pause: Rewrite Y and Z over 0 to 1, showing each width factor.

recall.reminder: Track the new input and the new height separately when you stretch a graph.

hints.title: Compare the powers of 2
hints.body: Write every resulting height as a power of 2. Compare the exponents when the input lies strictly between 0 and 1.
hints.recap: The larger exponent gives the larger height because the base is 2.
hints.pitfall: Equal heights at an endpoint do not mean equal areas.
hints.pause: Order the graph heights throughout the interval, then order the integrals.

recall.reminder: Compare x, its square and its square root using the allowed interval.
